title: Tensor comparison for locally closed finite-free generators
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] (quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]), let $\Lambda$ be any commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and put $R_Y=p_Y^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] for schemes $Y$ over $X$. Work on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] in ordinary unbounded derived categories of $R_Y$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], with relative derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ and $b:T\hookrightarrow X$ be constructible locally closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $L,M$ be $R_S$- and $R_T$-modules, respectively, each lisse [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module], meaning finite free on a pro-etale cover. Form the scheme-theoretic fibre product $W=S\times_XT$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $r:W\to S$, $s:W\to T$ and immersion $c=ar=bs:W\hookrightarrow X$. For every locally closed immersion $h$, use the exact functor $h_!$ defined by closed direct image and open extension by zero [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-weil-open-immersion], and exact inverse image $h^*$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] with pulled-back coefficients. There is a natural isomorphism
$$ (a_!L)[0]\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_X}(b_!M)[0]\ \cong\ c_!\bigl((r^*L\otimes_{R_W}s^*M)[0]\bigr). $$
The right-hand tensor is underived; $r^*L\otimes_{R_W}s^*M$ is finite free on a common pro-etale cover, of rank $mn$ wherever the two factors have ranks $m,n$. In particular the displayed object has cohomology only in degree zero and its degree-zero cohomology is constructible with finite constant local models [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: it is this finite free module on $W$ and has zero model off $W$. The isomorphism uses the actual scheme fibre product, with its pulled-back coefficients, and is independent of choices of open/closed factorizations up to the normalized extension comparisons. Empty intersections and rank zero are allowed. No coefficient admissibility, finite-type or base-field hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Immersions into the Noetherian scheme X have Noetherian, quasi-compact source, by their topological embedding and local finite type. Apply this also to the pullback immersions, the factors of either factorization and their complementary immersions. This supplies the quasi-compactness hypotheses in closed support and base change.

proof.text: Pull back the lisse trivializations along the two actual projections of S times_X T. Refine the covers by pairwise fibre products, using the generic local-freeness pullback and refinement lemmas. Exact monoidal inverse image and distributivity over finite biproducts identify the tensor with a finite free module of rank m*n, using the equivalence Fin m times Fin n = Fin (m*n). Zero ranks are included.

proof.text: For either order of factors, the actual open unit and closed counit give the restriction isomorphism, and the extension is fully faithful. The extension restricts to zero along disjoint morphisms. For closed-then-open factors use open base change and closed-complement vanishing; this holds for arbitrary source schemes. For open-then-closed factors use the closed ring-sheaf base-change mate and open-extension vanishing on the closed pullback.

proof.text: Call a module supported on a locally closed immersion if its restriction along every disjoint morphism from a quasi-compact Noetherian scheme vanishes. Successive open and closed support reconstruction identifies any such module N with the extension of its restriction, for either order of factors. Tensor preserves this support condition. The tensor of modules supported on a and b is supported on their actual fibre product: after a pullback disjoint from the intersection, reconstruct along the pullback of a and use the vanishing restriction of the other factor there. Consequently the ordinary tensor of the two extensions is an extension from the intersection. Normalize the comparison to the canonical monoidal restriction isomorphism. Full faithfulness and the restriction isomorphism show that restriction is injective on these Hom sets; this proves naturality and compatibility with every normalized extension comparison.

proof.text: Lisse modules are flat by locally finite free tensor exactness. Their extensions are flat too: for a monomorphism f, the kernel of tensoring f with the extension is supported on the same immersion, and its restriction vanishes by flatness of the lisse restriction and exact monoidal inverse image. Support reconstruction detects this kernel as zero. Right exactness of tensor then gives exactness.

source.place: Proof (1); support reconstruction replaces the two projection calculations below the unit level

proof.text: The single complex of a flat module is K-flat. The canonical lax monoidal comparison of localization is therefore invertible on the two single complexes. The tensor of two degree-zero complexes is canonically the single complex of their ordinary tensor; naturality follows by checking the (0,0) summand, with all other summands zero. Combine this natural comparison with the normalized ordinary comparison of step 4, and package the two variable naturality as an isomorphism of bifunctors. Its compatibility with normalized factorization comparisons follows from the same naturality and step 4.

proof.text: For the homology assertions choose a closed-then-open factorization of the actual intersection. The comparison identifies the tensor with a single complex, so all homology away from zero vanishes and H0 is its ordinary extension. A lisse module has a finite constant local model, and closed direct image and open extension preserve its finite constructible stratification. Transport that stratification along the H0 isomorphism. Restriction to the intersection is the specified open-unit/closed-counit isomorphism; restriction along every disjoint morphism, with arbitrary source, is zero by the closed-then-open vanishing of step 3.
